111: Ravina said: Combine and teach - the two baraitot quoted earlier are not meant to be taught individually. [That is, it is not meant] to be taught in the first quotation that "threshing" specifically implies something whose work is not complete with regard to tithes, because this would imply that if it were complete with regard to tithes [the worker] would not be able to eat; that would contradict the latter [ baraita]. Rather, combine and teach them as one: Just as "threshing" [grain] is specifically something whose work is not complete with respect to tithes and ḥalla -- which are laws pertinent to [grain] -- likewise for anything whose work is not complete with respect to laws pertinent to it: if with respect to tithes alone, then for tithes; if with respect to ḥalla, then for ḥalla [as well]. This excludes one who is separating dates [from being allowed to eat], which are already complete with regard to tithes, and for which there is no later [task]. This [also] excludes one who kneads, since its work -- the latter [of work with respect to tithes and work with respect to ḥalla] -- has been completed.
